## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Zìzàiwáng púsà jīng* in 2 fascicles is [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) Kumārajīva's Yáo Qín 姚秦 translation of the *Vikurvāṇa-rāja-paripṛcchā* — the questions posed to the Buddha by the bodhisattva *Zìzàiwáng* 自在王 (Skt. *Vikurvāṇa-rāja* "King of Self-Mastery"). The Taishō print signs the entry "姚秦三藏鳩摩羅什譯" and explicitly cross-references *No. 421* — [KR6h0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6h/KR6h0030), [瞿曇般若流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9E%BF%E6%9B%87%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) Gautama Prajñāruci's later 元魏 retranslation of the same Indic source under the alternative title *Fènxùnwáng wèn jīng* 奮迅王問經. The opening is the standard Mahāyāna setting at the *Anāthapiṇḍada-ārāma* in *Śrāvastī*, where the assembly of twenty thousand bhikṣus is gathered together with bodhisattvas-of-one-life-remaining including [彌勒](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%8C%E5%8B%92) Maitreya and [得大勢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%97%E5%A4%A7%E5%8B%A2) Mahāsthāmaprāpta.

**Abstract**

The *Vikurvāṇa-rāja-paripṛcchā* is one of [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) Kumārajīva's principal Mahāyāna sūtra translations of the Yáo-Qín period. The protagonist *Zìzàiwáng* / *Vikurvāṇa-rāja* — "King of Self-Mastery" or "King of the Magical Display" — questions the Buddha on the bodhisattva's *zìzài* 自在 (self-mastery/free-functioning) over phenomena: the four kinds of self-mastery, the practices that develop them, and the bodhisattva-bhūmis on which they are realised. The work belongs with the related *paripṛcchā* sūtras of the Mahāsaṃnipāta cycle and is one of the principal Indic Mahāyāna treatises on bodhisattva *vaśitā* (mastery).

The translation was produced at the *Cǎotáng* 草堂 monastery in Cháng'ān, in the Yáo-Qín period under the patronage of [姚興](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E8%88%88) Yáo Xīng. The dating window 401–413 reflects the bracket of [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80)'s most active Cháng'ān period, beginning with his arrival in 401 (Hóngshǐ 弘始 3) and ending with his death in 413 (Hóngshǐ 15). The *Chū sānzàng jì jí* 出三藏記集 (T2145) records the work in his catalogue.
